$comment: READ-ONLY, and the finer-grained half of the DQ read. A monitor says WHICH
columns are watched; a check says WHAT is being asserted about them — the
category, the metric, the operator and the threshold.
That distinction matters for the report. 'This element has a monitor' is a
weak statement. 'This element is checked for completeness but nothing tests
its accuracy, and the standard governing it requires a measured accuracy rate'
is the finding worth reporting, and it needs the checks, not the monitors.
`category` is exactly the vocabulary the regulation uses: accuracy,
completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness, custom. BCBS 239
names the same dimensions, so a requirement in a standard can be compared to a
CheckResponse carries NO reference to the DQ standard it came from — verified
2026-09-04. The UI shows a 'From standard' pill, but there is no standard_id
field and no from_standard filter, so an agent cannot tell whether a check was
created from a standard or by hand. Do not report on that; it is not knowable
PATCH on this path is a bare array, so checks are readable and not writable.
See the DQ section in CLAUDE.md before proposing otherwise.
name: Fetch DQ Checks
description: List the individual data quality checks running in this Alation instance — for each one the category (accuracy, completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness), the metric being measured, the operator and threshold, the table and column it runs against, and whether it is enabled. Use this to say what a column is actually tested for, rather than only whether some monitor covers it. Read-only.

ds_ids.description: Restrict to specific data sources, e.g. [2] for MCF Snowflake.

table_ids.description: Restrict to specific tables, by numeric table id.

monitor_ids.description: Restrict to the checks belonging to specific monitors.

category.description: Filter by check category: accuracy, completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness or custom. These are the same dimensions BCBS 239 names, so a category maps almost directly onto a standard's requirement.

metric_name.description: Filter by the metric being measured, e.g. missing_count.

enabled.description: Filter to enabled or disabled checks. A disabled check is not testing anything — worth reporting separately from an absent one.

limit.description: Maximum checks to return. Server maximum is 1000.
